chapter: Billy Pierce Studio and New York tap
title: Arriving at the Billy Pierce Studio and Eleanor Powell noticing him
summary: With Bradley gone to England, Green meets Eleanor Powell at the studio, who picks him to help with taps; he is about fifteen.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: That was 'Sweet Sue', the tap dance of Slim and Shorty. We got (inaudible) ahead, and the audience liked it, and so we, eventually we came to New York City and to Billy Pierce Studio at 46th Street. (Recording interruption) So we met Mr. Billy Pierce -- Mr. and Mrs. Billy Pierce rather -- and he put us in Mr. Buddy Bradley's studio, where Mr. Buddy Bradley used to teach. I didn't know Mr. Buddy Bradley wasn't going to be there. He told us that Mr. Buddy Bradley had went to Europe, went to England. And we stayed there in the studio for about -- about two weeks, you see, and I met Miss Eleanor Powell there. She was a student of Buddy Bradley, and I -- something good happened for her, see. She was captain of the chorus line at the Paramount Theater there in New York City, and she used to come up to 46th Street, you know, between shows and take lessons from Mr. Buddy Bradley.

But by him not being there, she saw me. I was asking Slim another question about tap dancing, and she told Mr. Pierce that she had gotten a break or something to the moving picture people. They wanted her to make a movie or something. This was without a screen test. You know, it was a rush job or something, and she would have to learn sound, you know, tap dancing.

She was already a great dancer. She was a champion dancer, but she had never did like the sound with the taps, you know, and she hadn't --- really hadn't put taps on her shoes. She had some favorite pair of shoes she liked to dance in. So she was getting taps on these shoes at the time that Mr. Buddy Bradley left. He went to England and Europe, you see.

And quite naturally, I don't think she knew this, and -- but she still liked to learn these things, this tap dancing, see. So she showed me some of the steps that -- rather she chose me. She asked Mr. Pierce, say, I like the way he dances, that one over there. She probably thought I was a teacher, you see. I was asking a question about tap dancing from my partner, Slim. See?
Well, you were just a little kid then, weren't you?
Yeah, I was a teenager. And, see, because we had aged some. We had stayed in Philadelphia with Edwina Sutton about two and a half years, at So, I was
approximately about 15 years old. I was going into the 15th year.
But, of course, you were progressing with your tap dancing all the time. I mean You just didn't sit around, I mean --

No. No. No, we danced, you know, because it was right in a dancing studio, you know, so we danced, learned new steps and things, and I was -- I was in that process at the time she looked over in the corner and saw me, see, and she says she wanted -- she liked the rhythm. Evidently, I must have been a natural dancer or something, you know, because I was in the process of learning how to dance on roller skates too, you see. I could tap dance on roller skates, and I was very --

-- versatile, see, at that time, see. But I -- I couldn't understand. I was trying to understand myself, you see, and I knew I loved rhythm. I knew -- I knew that. I loved rhythms. That's why she chose me, and she -- he gave her permission to take the lessons from me, you see, so -- for Mr. Buddy Bradley, see.
